classical Hurwitz lattice and Cayley-Hamilton identities
correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the integral quaternion-order basis (1,i,j,(1+i+j+k)/2), norm-3 doubled-coordinate parity equation and Cayley–Hamilton reduction of the unital generated subalgebra to Z-span{1,x,y,xy}. In standard coordinates determinant magnitude equals |U×V|²/16 and Hurwitz covolume is 1/2, giving exact generation criterion Q(U,V)=8. Possible imaginary squared lengths 3,8,11,12 force the successful pairs (3,3),(3,8),(3,11). An independent standard-library enumeration of all 96 norm-3 elements and all 9216 ordered pairs gives first-coordinate trace counts (16,24,48,8), partner counts (36,8,4,0), total 960. Unit group has 24 elements, and any simultaneous-conjugation stabilizer of a generating pair is central ±1; every orbit has 12 members and there are 80. This is exhaustive at norm 3 only.
residual_risks: Orbit count is under the 24-element inner unit group, not all automorphisms of all quaternion orders.
Our enumeration independently checks Q-based classification, not direct lattice Smith form for each pair; the index identity is separately derived analytically.

value.rationale: Norm 3 is the first prime-power level for the classical Hurwitz order, naturally singled out by the modern minimal-generator question. Exact incidence 960/9216, the unavoidable trace-3 coordinate and 80 symmetry orbits give a complete structural first-level census not entailed by existence alone.
residual_risks: Does not generalize to higher norms, other quaternion discriminants, or full automorphism group actions.

limitations: Classical integral Hurwitz order only, generators both norm3; conjugacy by units only.
